subject: Climate & Environment
title: Nitrogen Dioxide
description: A quick, practical guide to Nitrogen Dioxide.

hook.text: That brown haze hanging over a city skyline? Much of it is nitrogen dioxide.

buildup.text: Diesel engines, power plants, and factories release nitrogen oxides when fuel burns hot.

discovery.text: NO₂ inflames airways and increases vulnerability to respiratory infections.

twist.text: Children living near busy roads have measurably worse lung function than those who don't.

climax.text: Satellite maps show NO₂ plumes tracing highways and industrial zones from space.

punchline.text: Traffic jams are visible from orbit — painted in toxic gas.

quiz.question: What is a major source of nitrogen dioxide in cities?

details.summary: Nitrogen dioxide is a reddish-brown gas produced mainly by burning fossil fuels in vehicles and power plants. It irritates the airways, worsens asthma, and reacts with sunlight to create ground-level ozone and smog in urban areas.
details.whyItMatters: NO2 is a key marker of traffic-related pollution and a precursor to ozone and acid rain. Monitoring it helps cities design cleaner transport policies.
takeaways: NO2 comes primarily from vehicle engines and power stations
It triggers and worsens asthma and other respiratory conditions
It reacts in sunlight to form ground-level ozone and smog

faq.question: Why is nitrogen dioxide especially high near busy roads?
faq.answer: Vehicle engines combust fuel at high temperatures, splitting atmospheric nitrogen and oxygen into nitrogen oxides. Concentrations drop sharply within a few hundred meters of the roadway as gases disperse and react.

faq.question: How does nitrogen dioxide contribute to acid rain?
faq.answer: NO2 reacts with water vapor in the atmosphere to form nitric acid, which falls as acid rain. This acidifies lakes and soils, damages forests, and corrodes buildings and monuments over time.
